subject: Unexpected 'session stitching' line on Nov invoice — request for per-session audit
content:
From: Sarah Ng <sarah@glyphhealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, accounts@glyphhealth.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question about line on Nov invoice (INV-20261130)

Hi Laura,

We were reviewing our November invoice (INV-20261130) and found a new line item labeled 'session stitching' with a fairly large token count (see attached). That line doesn't match any of our expected usage patterns — it seems to have aggregated many short reconnects into a single higher-charge bucket.

Can you:
- Provide a per-session (session_id) audit for the entries contributing to that line for the period 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-30?
- Explain the billing logic used to compute the stitching multiplier and why these events were grouped?
- Confirm how VAT should be applied for this charge (we are EU-registered; our AP team needs the VAT treatment explicitly on the corrected invoice).

We attached the invoice and flagged lines we think are suspicious. If you need example session IDs we can export a few from our side — please let us know the preferred format.

Thanks,
Sarah
Accounts Payable | Glyph Health
Attachment: INV-20261130-GlyphHealth.pdf

---
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Ng <sarah@glyphhealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question about line on Nov invoice (INV-20261130)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the invoice. I can appreciate the urgency on VAT and AP timing.

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
1) I'll kick off a per-session audit with Billing/Infra to pull the raw events that contributed to the 'session stitching' aggregate. Markus/Neha will own the reconciliation and provisional credit if we find misattribution.
2) Michael will coordinate timing with your AP and confirm whether a VAT-corrected invoice is required or we can issue a credit + replacement invoice.
3) We aim to deliver an initial audit report (sample of 250 session ids + how they were counted) within 3 business days and a full reconciliation within 7 business days.

Two quick asks for your team to speed things up:
- If you can export three representative session IDs where you saw repeated reconnects (format: session_id	start_ts	user_id) that would help us focus the sampling.
- Confirm whether your entity expects a VAT-inclusive invoice or prefers a net invoice with reverse-charge annotation.

I'm attaching a small sample export we use for internal review so you can see the columns we'll provide.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_usage_sample_202611.csv

---
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Ng <sarah@glyphhealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question about line on Nov invoice (INV-20261130)

Sarah / Laura — I pulled the raw stitch logs for November and attached a short extract (stitching_log_2026-11.csv) and a quick explanatory note below.

What we found (summary):
- The 'session stitching' line is produced by our post-processing that compresses multiple short-lived socket reconnects (same session metadata) into a single session to avoid double-counting prefix tokens. In most cases this reduces billable tokens.
- In Glyph's dataset for Nov, a subset of sessions had interleaved reconnects across distinct connections that our heuristic currently treats as separate logical conversations, causing the post-processor to re-aggregate those into stitched sessions during the billing window. The effect increased token attribution for ~0.6% of sessions, concentrated on a handful of long-running test feeds.

Sample calc for one stitched session (from stitch log extract):
- raw_token_sum_before_stitch = 18,742
- tokens_removed_by_prefix_cache = 1,128
- final_tokens_after_stitch = 21,392
- effective multiplier observed = final / raw_before ≈ 1.142

This behavior can be argued both ways — in some workloads stitching reduces duplicates, in others it ends up combining partial transcripts and inflating the final tally. Given this unexpected impact for you, we propose:
1) A provisional credit equal to 75% of the delta attributable to stitching while we complete a full session-level audit. That would appear as a credit on a corrected invoice.
2) A post-audit correction (if the audit finds our heuristic in error on specific session groups) to fully reconcile either with a further credit or reversal.
3) VAT handling: because Glyph Health is an EU-registered entity and the service is delivered remotely, we should annotate the corrected invoice with reverse-charge wording and zero-rate VAT on the line, pending your confirmation of VAT registration number. If your AP prefers a VAT-inclusive corrected invoice, we can reissue accordingly.

I've attached the stitch log snippet for transparency. We can also provide a row-level CSV with session_ids, original_token_counts, and final_token_counts.

Provisional credit calculation example in CSV: see attached stitch_log_2026-11.csv (col: session_id, delta_tokens, delta_cost_usd).

We'll hold off collection on this line until the audit completes — Michael, please ensure collections are paused for INV-20261130 line 'session stitching' and flag the invoice as under dispute.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachment: stitching_log_2026-11.csv

---
From: Sarah Ng <sarah@glyphhealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: accounts@glyphhealth.com, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question about line on Nov invoice (INV-20261130)

Hi Markus / Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the transparency in the stitch extract. We ran the three session IDs you highlighted against our logs and they match the reconnect pattern we expected — looks like the heuristic re-aggregated distinct test connections.

Glyph Health requests:
- Please apply the provisional credit as proposed and provide a revised invoice with the reverse-charge VAT annotation (our VAT reg: GH-EU-44577).
- Send the full audit CSV (session_id, original_tokens, final_tokens, delta_tokens, delta_cost_usd) as soon as available so our internal finance team can close the AP hold.

Once we have the corrected invoice with VAT annotation we will release the payment for the remainder of the balance.

Appreciate the collaboration — Sarah
Accounts Payable | Glyph Health
